(a) adaptive frame rate control can be used effectively to reduce the effects of network jitter and congestion on real time packet video; (b) adaptive frame rate and transport flow control can be integrated effectively to provide robustness to the network; and (c) the adaptive frame rate and flow control algorithms are portable and can be used on a variety of workstation platforms with minimal changes

(1) a simple and robust feedback mechanism for adaptive rate control is possible in workstation environments, (2) the mechanism is robust enough to handle the wide variety of network and system loads that are likely to be experienced, and (3), the mechanism can provide graceful tradeoffs between resolution and loss rates.
(a) the proposed feedback control system can achieve good jitter control by gracefully trading image quality, and that (b) flow control can reduce loss rates by a factor of 10 or more.

the design and implementation of a portable, responsive, and robust software mechanism that can be used to control the presentation and transport layer frame rates of real-time packet video transfer and display in a workstation environment.
the design of a portable and robust adaptive frame rate control mechanism for real time packetized video transfer and display.

the design and evaluation of an adaptive control mechanism that allows the presentation layer of a packet video system to dynamically adjust its frame rate and image resolution in order to provide a robust and responsive service in the face of network congestion.
